source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46 Total Pensions and Annuities; FAQ 'Is retirement income taxable?'; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46 early or excess distributions (Federal Form 5329); Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Subpart 02 Chapter 07 rules 100, 101 and 104 (https://www.sos.ms.gov/adminsearch/ACCode/00000158c.pdf, PDF p.18)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 30,000.00 = 30,000.00. Federal taxable income = 30,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction = 14,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 30,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Projection: less retirement income 30,000.00 (ms_retirement_income_exempt covers ira_distribution at every age; it cannot tell an early distribution). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 0.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 6,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 0.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = -8,300.00 on the formula; floored at 0.00 (the form enters 0). Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1 to 4 and line 17 = 0.00. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 0.00. The form: person 0 is 50, under 59 1/2, and the inputs give no federal exception, so the distribution is early (Form 5329). Regulation rule 104: early distributions do not qualify for the exemption and are subject to state income tax (no state early withdrawal penalty). Line 46 would carry 30,000.00; line 13 Mississippi AGI 30,000.00; line 16 taxable 30,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 6,000.00 = 21,700.00; Schedule of Tax Computation: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00, remaining 11,700.00 x 4.4% = 514.80; line 20 = 514.80 (whole dollars 515). The projection understates by 514.80, as its approximation says. There is no pension item, so the has_pension marker does not fire and the run gives no Mississippi warning here.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

IRA, 401(k), 403(b) and 457 payouts and Roth conversions are exempted at every age. Mississippi exempts them only when they are not early distributions (regulation rule 104), and a deferred compensation payout only once the person qualifies for other retirement income by minimum age, years of service or other criteria (rule 102). A projection cannot test either, so an early payout is exempted here; the warning names it for anyone under 60.
